tagline: Out of Fairbanks to the gold camps and the Yukon.
intro: The Steese leaves Fairbanks past Fox and runs northeast through gold country, completed in 1927 to serve the Circle Mining District, which was busy in the 1890s, before the Klondike. Felix Pedro's 1902 strike, which started Fairbanks, the preserved gold camp at Chatanika and working dredges all line the road. Much of it is narrow and winding.
Eagle Summit is the place for the midnight sun at the June solstice. Around Central the pavement ends, after about 81 miles, and the rest is dirt and gravel to the Yukon.

moments.title: Gold Dredge Number 8
moments.text: A five-deck dredge 250 feet long, kept as a National Historic Site on ground that has yielded more than 7.5 million ounces of gold.

moments.title: Central
moments.text: In one of the state's most active mining districts, the Circle District Historical Society museum keeps pre-glacial mammal remains found in Mammoth Creek.

moments.title: Circle
moments.text: The miners who named it believed they were on the Arctic Circle, about 50 miles short, and before the Klondike it was the biggest settlement on the Yukon.

practical: Paved for about the first 81 miles, then dirt and gravel from around Central. The road has closure gates, so check 511 Alaska before driving through to Circle.
